risks.risk: Unknown make, model, and capacity (cavities, output rate, bottle size range) which drives price heavily in industrial equipment.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the manufacturer's nameplate/serial tag, usually on the frame or control box.
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest end of generic small-capacity single-cavity machines

risks.risk: Missing or damaged mold(s) — a bottle blow machine without a compatible mold is far less valuable.
risks.proof: Photo of the mold(s) included with the sale, mounted or separate.

risks.risk: Electrical/control panel condition and completeness (PLC, sensors, wiring) cannot be assessed from one static photo.

risks.if_unproven: priced as control system unverified/possibly faulty

risks.risk: Machine age, hours of use, and maintenance history unknown.
risks.proof: Photos of any service/maintenance log or visible date/serial on tag.

proof_requests: Video of the machine running a complete molding cycle, from feed to finished bottle.
Close-up photo of the manufacturer's nameplate with brand, model, and serial number.
Photo of the mold(s) included, if any.
Photo/video of the control panel powered on.
Wide shots from multiple angles showing the full machine, plus any visible wear, rust, or missing parts.
response.reason: The single photo shows a plausible PET bottle blow molding machine but no nameplate, no running demonstration, and no mold — without at least the nameplate/specs or a working video, even a worst-case price cannot be anchored to a real category of this wide-ranging industrial equipment.
